stories.headline: FDA chief Tukaram flags huge price gaps in medical devices, seeks Centre’s intervention
stories.deck: The report cited that an IV set purchased for ₹11.05 had a declared MRP of ₹325, while an infusion set purchased for ₹11 had an MRP of ₹201.
stories.bodyText:
Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Commissioner Tukaram Munde has initiated action to focus on the drug part of FDA as he has written to the Department of Pharmaceuticals and National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), recommending guidelines on the permissible gap between trade procurement and MRP.
Calling the gap a core public health issue, Mr. Munde said, “The most expensive part of a hospital bill may never touch the hospital at all. A patient admitted for care has no way of knowing whether the price on a medical consumable reflects its actual cost or a markup fixed long before it ever reached the ward.“
Mr. Munde pointed out that the review of the findings of the survey and clear guidelines on the permissible gap between trade procurement price and declared MRP have been recommended to the Department of Pharmaceuticals and the NPPA, and this is not just to close a pricing gap, but also the information gap patients have.
A survey of hospital consumables in Maharashtra found an IV infusion set with a trade price of ₹11.05 carrying a printed MRP of ₹325, a markup of 2,841%. A syringe procured at ₹6.75 carried an MRP of ₹57.20. A catheter procured at ₹29.41 carried an MRP of ₹310.
Explaining the gap and need for transparency, he said on X that as they are not elective purchases, patients cannot compare prices, seek alternatives, or question the MRP while receiving care.
“The MRP itself is often fixed upstream by manufacturers and distributors, disconnected from the trade price by a wide, unexplained margin. The result is a system where the party bearing the cost has the least information to evaluate it,” he added.
The regulatory gap is structural: scheduled medicines are capped under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013. Most medical devices and consumables are not covered, leaving both the pricing and the information around it almost entirely unmonitored, he added on X.

stories.headline: At least 33 illegal mining suspects found dead in Nigerian custody with officials blaming disease
stories.deck: 65 detainees were packed into a poorly ventilated cell, suggesting the dead may have suffocated; bodies have been sent to a local hospital for “further medical examination to establish the actual cause of death"
stories.bodyText:
At least 33 suspects arrested for alleged illegal mining were found dead in Nigerian security custody on Thursday (September 17, 2026), officials said, claiming a suspected disease outbreak was to blame.
But Dauda Shehu, a survivor of the incident, said that 65 detainees were packed into a poorly ventilated cell, suggesting the dead may have suffocated.
The detainees died in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defense Corps, or NSCDC, in north-central Niger state, its spokesperson Abubakar Muti said.
From 2025: Conflict, poverty, climate change fuel Nigeria’s worsening malnutrition crisis
They had been in detention since the security agency carried out arrests on Tuesday and Wednesday (September 15-16) over suspicion of illegal mining in the state, head of the NSCDC in Niger Suberu Siyaka Aniviye said in a statement.
Mr. Aniviye said while the agency suspects a disease, the detainees' bodies have been sent to a local hospital for “further medical examination to establish the actual cause of death.” He did not elaborate on the type of disease.
“We were jampacked and there was no ventilation for us to breathe well,” said Shehu, the survivor. “All of a sudden, we realized that we could not breathe and we started scrambling to get fresh air.”
Mr. Shehu, who spoke to AP at the Minna General Hospital where the bodies were sent for examination, said the detainees tried to get the attention of the security agency's guards by banging on the cell door.
Shafatu Sulaiman lost her two sons in the incident. Speaking to the AP at the Minna Hospital over their bodies, she pleaded for the government to intervene.
Police in Niger state said they have launched an investigation and urged relatives of the victims to come forward with any information that could help.
Illegal mining remains a challenge in Nigeria. Analysts have linked illegal mining activities in Nigeria's north-central and northwest regions to armed gangs involved in kidnappings for ransom, claiming groups receive funding from the illicit trade. (AP)

stories.headline: SC takes exception to 31 unnatural deaths in Manipur relief camps
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday took strong exception to 31 unnatural deaths in Manipur's relief camps - set up after the eruption of Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes in 2023 to shelter internally displaced persons (IDPs) - including one due to sexual assault.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the state govt to file an affidavit giving details of the causes of death as ascertained through postmortem reports and the investigations to identify the culprits. It also questioned the state for giving a meagre Rs 30,000 as compensation to the next of kin even though the state had paid Rs 4 lakh-5 lakh to relatives of victims of the ethnic clashes.
This order was passed after perusing Justice Gita Mittal Committee's report. Placed before the court by senior advocate Vibha D Makhija, it cited a TOI report of June 7 which published a news report on 731 deaths, including 25 unnatural deaths, in relief camps as disclosed by the state home department. TOI had also reported that 43,000 IDPs were residing in various relief camps.
Makhija said when the committee sought details of the deaths, the state initially provided sketchy statistics. 
Only after prodding did govt provide the required information. Jiribam and Churachandpur relief camps recorded nine unnatural deaths each; six were reported in Bishnupur, four in Imphal West, two in Imphal East and one in Kakching.
The bench directed the state chief secretary to submit what remedial measures would be taken to prevent such incidents. It also asked the state to detail the steps taken to expedite investigations into the FIRs.

In Kangpokpi relief camp, where 128 IDPs died natural deaths, no compensation was paid to their kin, it said.

stories.headline: Centre agrees to lower cut-off for NEET-SS admission
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Nudged by Supreme Court to reduce the cut-off percentile for admission to super specialty medical courses to fill around 2,000 vacant seats, Centre Thursday told the court that the qualifying percentile for NEET-SS may go from the existing 50th to 30th for the proposed special stray vacancy round, to be conducted soon, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.
SC last week asked govt to reconsider its decision not to reduce the cut-off percentile in order to ensure seats were not wasted. Govt filed a two-page note before a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe and said "the matter has since been reconsidered in consultation with stakeholders concerned".
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
"In order to ensure available super specialty seats do not remain vacant and that the available training capacity is optimally utilised, it has been decided that the qualifying percentile for NEET-SS may be reduced from existing 50th percentile to 30th percentile for the purpose of proposed special stray vacancy round," govt said.
It, however, told SC those students who had already taken admission would not be allowed to participate in the special stray vacancy round. It proposed the round "be conducted strictly in accordance with the existing principles or rules applicable to a stray vacancy round, with no provision for upgradation of candidates who are already holding/joined a seat", govt said.
After the second round of NEET-SS counselling, 1,857 super specialty seats - including 1,094 DM/MCh seats and 763 DNB-SS seats - were vacant. A substantial number of these pertain to highly specialised medical and surgical disciplines.

briefs.headline: HAL airport becomes first in India to operationalise RNP CAT H helicopter approach
briefs.deck: RNP CAT H helicopter approach procedure is a satellite-guided precision navigation system designed exclusively for helicopters
briefs.bodyText:
The Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) airport in Bengaluru has become the first airport in India to operationalise the Required Navigation Performance – Category H (RNP CAT H) helicopter approach procedure.
RNP CAT H helicopter approach procedure is a satellite-guided precision navigation system designed exclusively for helicopters.
Also Read: HAL cannot do everything alone, private sector crucial to aerospace ecosystem: CMD Ravi K.
Developed in India
Developed by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), validated through flight trials by HAL test pilots, and approved by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), this approach allows helicopters to fly highly accurate optimised paths, enabling all-weather access while safely navigating terrain and urban obstacles. The procedure reduces the approach time to HAL airport from 12 minutes to about four minutes.
Enhances safety
“This capability enhances the safety, efficiency and accessibility of helicopter operations, and establishes a benchmark for similar procedures to be implemented in airports across the country,” said Ravi K., CMD, HAL.
This system enhances operational efficiency and airspace capacity, enables seamless integration of rotary and fixed-wing operations, reduces noise footprint over cities, and provides faster, safer routes for critical missions such as air ambulance and rescue operations.
50 helicopter movements every day
Though the HAL airport stopped commercial operations in 2008 following opening of the Kempegowda International Airport, it continues to be used for military flight testing and charter flight operations.
Among other things, HAL airport handles nearly 50 helicopter movements every day. HAL has closed a long-standing gap in India’s aviation infrastructure with this launch, paving the way for safer, smarter helicopter operations, according to the company.

briefs.headline: After brief disruption, officials restart talks for Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman’s India visit
briefs.deck: Sources in Dhaka said efforts are underway to schedule his visit to New Delhi during a suitable period in November following Mr. Rahman’s existing diplomatic engagements
briefs.bodyText:
After a brief disruption in ties, India and Bangladesh have resumed official-level talks to firm up plans for a visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to New Delhi, diplomatic sources have confirmed.
Bilateral relations took a hit after the virtual press conference by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in August triggered backlash in her home country. Ms. Hasina is currently living in an undisclosed location in India.
The Hindu was told that officials on both sides have continued meetings in Dhaka and are working on setting up an agenda for the visit that will include regularisation of bilateral trade that has been affected because of unstable political relations and questions over the renewal of Ganga Water Treaty among other issues.
Also Read | ‘Rahman wants to visit India, but agenda has to be set first’
Envoy’s meetings
Sources in Dhaka said Prime Minister Mr. Rahman is scheduled to travel to New York for the United Nations General Assembly this month following which he will have multiple diplomatic engagements over October and November, while efforts are underway to schedule his visit to New Delhi during a suitable window in November. Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi has held meetings with a series of officials over the last few days, including the country’s Minister of Water Resources Mohammed Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee and Adviser to the Prime Minister for Ministry of Education Mahdi Amin.
Mr. Rahman was invited to participate in the recently held BRICS Summit here in his capacity as the head of BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) but Bangladesh did not send any representation to the event with Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir asserting that Bangladesh is planning to “reset” ties with India and for that Dhaka will prioritise a bilateral visit at a “conducive” moment. The Hindu had earlier reported that the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government had viewed the cancellation of a programme by supporters of Ms. Hasina’s Awami League earlier this month as a “positive sign”.
Ms. Hasina has been based in India since fleeing Dhaka on August 5, 2024 and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bangladesh had expressed “outrage” over her latest press conference where she had alleged that law and order had broken down in Bangladesh. Over the past two years, Ms. Hasina and several of her top ministers and officials have received death sentences at the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka for their alleged role in the crackdown against protesters in July-August 2024, which ultimately toppled her government.
Also Read | Rashtrapati Bhavan withdraws email on Bangladesh PM visit
Rahman’s emissaries
Though the fall of Ms. Hasina was seen as unexpected, sources within the current dispensation in Dhaka have said that Mr. Rahman maintained his touch with India during his years in exile in London and that he had received indication in February 2024 that New Delhi too was not expecting the Hasina government to last beyond a few months.
The Hindu was informed that Mr. Rahman’s personal contacts with Indian officials were renewed at least since February 2024 when he had sent an emissary to India to sense India’s mood following the widely criticised election of January 2024 that was boycotted by the BNP under his leadership. The engagement was in line with previous exchanges between BNP and India during the Sheikh Hasina era between 2009 and 2024 when she was in power.
Two months before the January 2024 election, current Energy Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku had visited New Delhi. In an interview with The Hindu, Mr. Tuku had urged India to extend “unambiguous support to the democratic aspirations” of the people of Bangladesh. In similar vein in 2018, a three-member team consisting of Abdul Awal Mintoo, Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury and Humayan KobirThe Daily Star had reported that the 2018 visit was a result of Mr. Rahman’s instruction to his party to carry out course correction as “the hostile policy towards India was wrong and misguided”.

briefs.headline: Former Minister Ram Asrey Kushwaha joins Samajwadi Party
briefs.deck: The Samajwadi Party government will be formed after the 2027 Assembly polls, and the rule of social justice will be established, says SP chief Akhilesh Yadav while reacting to the leader joining the party.
briefs.bodyText:
Former Minister and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Ram Asrey Kushwaha joined the Samajwadi Party (SP) on Thursday (September 17, 2026).
The Samajwadi Party said the joining will strengthen the party’s outreach among PDA social groups. PDA acronym stands for ‘Pichhde’ (backward classes), Dalits and ‘Alpsankhyak’ (minorities), but at times the SP leadership added other social groups to the plank.
Mr Kushwaha, a prominent leader from the Kushwaha social group, has also served as an office-bearer of ‘Kushwaha Kalyan Parishad’, a social organisation working for the social group that falls under the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) category.
He was associated with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and the SP in the past. Apart from Mr. Kushwaha, many political workers from other parties, like Vijay Kumar Singh from Aligarh, Anshu Dubey from Kannauj, Anoop Kashyap Pradhan, Nishad Party district president Kannauj, and Manoj Kumar Nishad, joined the Samajwadi Party.
All of them resolved to form the Samajwadi Party government in the 2027 Assembly elections. The SP president Akhilesh Yadav welcomed all the leaders, adding that the joining will strengthen the Samajwadi Party and PDA movement.
“Mr. Kushwaha is a senior leader, the joining will strengthen the party and the PDA movement. The Samajwadi Party government will be formed after the 2027 Assembly polls, and the rule of social justice will be established,” said Mr Yadav.
“The joining of the Samajwadi Party by Ram Asrey Kushwaha, a former minister and senior OBC leader, after 13 years in the BJP is testimony that OBC leaders are feeling suffocated in the BJP. It’s a simple message that the first and foremost precondition is respect in political parties, which is lacking in the BJP for OBCs and SCs. Home coming of Kushwaha and other leaders will boost the PDA movement and provide momentum to the Samajwadi Party in consolidating votes for the 2027 Assembly elections,” said Sudhir Panwar, a senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader.

briefs.headline: Rajasthan order asking students to join PM Modi's birthday celebrations sparks controversy
briefs.deck: Congress leader Tika Ram Jully asked why the government departments and educational institutions were being involved in PM Modi’s birthday celebrations.
briefs.bodyText:
The Opposition Congress and civil rights groups in Rajasthan on Thursday (September 17, 2026) took exception to a government order asking the college students to participate in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday celebrations. As many as 12 diverse activities will be organised during the month-long celebrations.
One of the events listed in the programme is ‘Ashirwad Ka Diya’ (lamp of blessings), in which the students, beneficiaries of government schemes and the public at large have been asked to light the lamps at dusk on the inaugural day of the ‘Viksit Bharat-Jan Seva Abhiyan’.
The Commissionerate of College Education has instructed all government and private colleges across the State to organise the events for lighting of lamps on September 17, community service on October 2 and ‘Seva First’ innovation challenge competitions for a fortnight from October 1 to 15, followed by submission of compliance reports.
College Education Commissioner Nathmal Didel said in the order that the month-long programme would be conducted on the basis of guidelines issued by the Planning Department. “The campaign is aimed at promoting public service, social concern and good governance,” Mr. Didel said.
Some of the private colleges in Jaipur reportedly asked the male members of their staff to stay put to light the lamps after the female teachers expressed their inability to remain present till late evening.
The Planning Department’s order stated that the campaign would be monitored through a dedicated portal, requiring the district administration and departments to upload details of programmes, photographs and videos. It said the information about government welfare activities would be spread and the participation of women, farmers and youth encouraged.
Congress leader Tika Ram Jully asked why the government departments and educational institutions were being involved in Mr. Modi’s birthday celebrations. “The [ruling] Bharatiya Janata Party wants to hide its colossal failures through such extravagant events. This despite the common people and vulnerable sections grappling with rising inflation and difficult circumstances,” Mr. Jully, the Leader of Opposition, said.
The People’s Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) said the BJP government had crossed “all limits of sycophancy” by officially celebrating Mr. Modi’s birthday. “Celebrating the birthdays of living, active politicians is a form of sycophancy that imprisons students in the archaic mindset of the feudal era. Institutions of higher learning should foster independent thinking and scientific temper among students,” PUCL national president Kavita Srivastava said.
PUCL State president Anant Bhatnagar regretted that the ruling BJP was forcing the college students to become “submissive subjects” rather than developing a critical vision among them. The PUCL termed the government order “authoritarian” and said no attempts should be made to stifle independent thinking of students.

briefs.headline: Why was Shahzad Bhatti Network designated as a terrorist group under UAPA? | Explained
briefs.deck: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said in a notification that the Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN), through its terrorist activities, poses a “serious threat to the democratic system, communal harmony, and internal security of the country”
briefs.bodyText:
The story so far: On September 16, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) designated the Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN) as a terrorist group under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The MHA said in a notification that the outfit, through its terrorist activities, poses a “serious threat to the democratic system, communal harmony, and internal security of the country”.
Who is Shahzad Bhatti?
Shahzad Bhatti, a social-media influencer and a Pakistani gangster is said to be the prime suspect behind the arrest of over 200 suspects in a countrywide counter-terror operation across the country ahead of Independence Day. Bhatti, who speaks Punjabi and regularly posts video on Instagram and Facebook, currently operates from the UAE, and over the past one-year has graduated from “organised crime” to “terror-related activities”. Several of his Instagram accounts ending in “333” have been flagged by security agencies. Before the pre-Independence Day pan-India raids and arrests against the SBN, Delhi Police had blocked 125 Instagram accounts related to Bhatti.
Detailing the reach of the network, Dehi Police said that since October 2025, the police registered 15 FIRs and arrested 69 accused, two-thirds from Punjab and U.P. Most were poorly educated, economically vulnerable individuals recruited via social media for money, Gulf relocation, or resolving personal issues. Monetary incentives generally outweighed ideology, police said. Multiple handlers assigned recruits tasks including reconnaissance, attacks, funding and logistics. The network’s Delhi-NCR targets included security personnel, political offices, businesses and activists. The police identified 108 raid targets, initiated proceedings against 35 and recovered grenades, pistols, cartridges, petrol bombs, CCTV cameras and SIM cards.
His earliest association with criminal activities in India started from Punjab and it soon spread across 14 States — Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, Punjab, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Karnataka, Gujarat, Bihar, Telangana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Kerala.
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has registered three cases allegedly involving Bhatti.
What does the latest notification under UAPA entail?
Union Home Minister Amit Shah said in a post on X on September 16, “Pursuing PM Shri @narendramodi Ji’s vision of zero tolerance against terror, the MHA declares the Shahzad Bhatti Network as a terrorist organisation under the UAPA.”
SBN is the 46th outfit to be designated as a “terrorist organisation” under the UAPA.
The designation has been made under Section 35 (I) of the UAPA, 1967 which empowers the MHA to designate an outfit as a “terrorist organisation”.
The other outfits in the list include — Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM), United National Liberation Front (UNLF), Kangleipak Communist Party, All Tripura Tiger Force, Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI), Communist Party of India (Marxizt-Leninst) – Peoples War, all its formations and front organisations among others.
Does the notification mention specific cases against SBN?
Without mentioning the specific cases against the network, the notification listed nine categories of crimes registered under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Information Technology Act, 2000, Explosives Substances Act, UAPA, the Official Secrets Act, 1923 (OSA), the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 and the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, 2007.
MHA said that SBN is an organisation whose objective is to involve gullible youth and local criminals to smuggle arms, explosives, and narcotics from across the border, and through terrorist activities, pose a serious threat to the democratic system, communal harmony, and internal security of the country. It added that “several criminal cases” have been duly registered against the cadres of SBN across multiple jurisdictions for their involvement in unlawful and terrorist activities.
It further said that SBN is involved in radicalising gullible youth by offering various allurements, motivating them for anti-national activities, and mobilising resources for anti-national acts in collusion with other banned organisations and designated entities.
“SBN is promoting terrorism through violent activities that disrupt public order and by using various digital communication platforms to disseminate provocative messages, posing a serious challenge to the integrity of the nation...the Central Government believes that ‘Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN)’ is involved in terrorism and has participated in various acts of terrorism in India,” the notification said.

briefs.headline: Tamil Nadu must change mindset, allow Hindi in schools: SC
briefs.deck: The Supreme Court has urged Tamil Nadu to rethink its position on Hindi education, emphasizing that states should not operate like separate nations. The bench called for discussions with the Centre about Navodaya Vidyalayas. Tamil Nadu's resistance is based on its two-language policy that diverges from this approach. The hearing is set to resume in December.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday told Tamil Nadu govt that it needed to change its mindset towards teaching Hindi in schools and should thrash out issues with Centre on setting up Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.
As Vijay-led TN govt took the same stand taken by the previous DMK govt, a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and A G Masih said individual states could not act like countries. "You have to change your mindset, it can't be that Hindi will not be taught on the soil of TN," the bench said.
TN has been opposing the setting up of these schools as they follow a three-language policy, including Hindi, which is against the state's two-language policy.
"We are saying in addition to all the good things you're doing in your state, having something in addition will not bring down your standards... People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," SC said.
Senior advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for the state, submitted it was against the federal structure to impose Centre's decision on a state. "It is against the state policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of Constitution. 
It is not a central govt school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate," he said.
Gupta submitted that cooperative federalism would never work in only one direction and such a policy should not be enforced by the court.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
The bench asked the state to comply with its order and posted the case for further hearing in Dec. SC had last Dec directed TN to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in each district within six weeks.
"We are not asking you to acquire land. We are only asking you to identify it... There is a need for dialogue. You can't say I won't accept a policy. Today it is education, tomorrow it will be something else. You have to relax this rigidity in your mind," SC said.
The court was hearing TN's plea challenging a Madras HC judgement directing it to set up Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district. HC had ruled that Navodaya Vidyalayas did not violate Tamil Nadu Tamil Learning Act and the state's blanket refusal to set up such schools curtailed students' right to choose educational institutions.

stories.headline: ‘I’ll make you vanish into Pakistan’: Bengaluru woman alleges harassment, threats
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A woman’s chance meeting with a man during a trip to 
Tamil Nadu
 in July turned into friendship in Bengaluru within days. In weeks, the man started allegedly harassing her, threatening to kill her and make her “disappear into Pakistan” if she ended their friendship. He claimed he was an undercover police officer to threaten her.
According to a complaint filed by 35-year-old 
Sukanya
 (name changed), private firm employee and from Bellandur, she became friends with 
Naresh
 (name changed) during her Kodaikanal trip from July 9 to 11.
On returning to Bengaluru, the two reconnected. Shockingly, Naresh would behave obscenely. When she refused to continue the relationship, the man abused her in public and confined her inside a hotel room. As she started avoiding him and blocked his number, he allegedly harassed her through fake email IDs and phone numbers and spread allegations portraying her as a “call girl”, her complaint stated.
According to Sukanya, Naresh claimed he was the narcotics division of the police department.

stories.headline: 3,756 cases booked against private buses after steep fare plaints in Karnataka
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 RTOs across 
Karnataka
 booked 3,756 cases against private bus operators and seized 33 vehicles during a five-day enforcement drive against overcharging and other violations.
The transport department had received several complaints about private operators charging exorbitant fares during the Ganesha Chaturthi season. In one instance, passengers were reportedly charged Rs 7,000 for travelling from Bengaluru to Hubballi.
Between Sept 11 and 15, RTO officials inspected 14,987 private buses, including inter-state services. Cases were booked for violations including permit rules, charging excess fares and tax evasion. Officials collected Rs 73.6 lakh, including Rs 40.3 lakh in penalties.
MP Omkareshwari, additional commissioner for transport (enforcement, South & Bengaluru Urban), said the drive was launched following complaints from the public. “During document verification and inspections, officials found several violations and took action accordingly. Complaints received from the public have been forwarded to the respective registering authorities for further action.”
Officials also found operators violating rules while transporting passengers’ luggage.
Overcharging by private bus operators during festive seasons has become a recurring issue, with passengers, particularly those travelling during weekends and holidays, often complaining of steep fares.

stories.headline: Man attacks wife with machete, suspected acid in Bengaluru’s J.P. Nagar
stories.bodyText:
A 26-year-old woman was allegedly attacked with a machete and had a suspected acidic substance poured on her by her husband near a private clinic in J.P. Nagar in south Bengaluru on Thursday.
The incident occurred around 9.15 a.m. when the victim, Madhumita, stepped out of the clinic where she worked to have breakfast. The accused, identified as Venkatesan, allegedly attacked her with a machete and then poured a liquid believed to be acid on her before attempting to flee.
The attack, which took place near the basement parking area of the clinic, was captured on mobile phones by onlookers.
Though bystanders tried to catch him, Venkatesan fled for some distance before a Bengaluru Traffic Police sub-inspector intercepted and detained him. He was later handed over to the J.P. Nagar police.
Preliminary investigations revealed that Venkatesan, a native of Tamil Nadu, married Madhumita, who hails from West Bengal, about three years ago in Madurai. However, the couple had been living separately for the past year following marital discord. While Venkatesan, who had been working in Bengaluru, recently moved to Tamil Nadu after taking up a new job, Madhumita continued to work at the private clinic and stayed in a paying guest accommodation in south Bengaluru.
According to the police, Venkatesan arrived in the city on his motorcycle on Wednesday night and waited near the clinic for Madhumita before attacking her on Thursday morning. Madhumita is in a critical condition and is undergoing treatment in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU).
A senior police officer said preliminary investigations indicated that the liquid poured on Madhumita had acidic properties. However, Scene of Crime officers have collected samples and sent them to the Forensic Science Laboratory to determine whether it was industrial acid or a floor-cleaning agent. Based on the report, the police will trace its source, the officer said.
The police suspect the attack stemmed from a marital dispute but are yet to ascertain the exact motive. The J.P. Nagar police have registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and launched an investigation.

stories.headline: Bengaluru: Two police officers suspended over video showing them collecting cash
stories.bodyText:
The East Division police have suspended two policemen who were allegedly caught on video accepting money from a shopkeeper in a narrow lane in K.G. Halli earlier this week.
The incident came to light after a passerby recorded the two policemen, who were in uniform and travelling on a motorcycle, allegedly taking money from a person believed to be a shopkeeper. aarti

Rahul Mishra, Brookefield resident

briefs.headline: Half of east Bengaluru PGs operate illegally: GBA tells HC
briefs.deck: Court Issues Safety Guidelines
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Nearly half of private paying guest accommodations (PGs) in east Bengaluru, the city’s tech corridor, are operating illegally. A Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) counsel informed the high court that out of 5,000 PGs in east Bengaluru, nearly 2,500 are run without a proper licence, plan sanction or fire safety requirements.
Notices are being issued to all of them, caveats will be filed both in HC and the jurisdictional civil courts, and efforts will be made to pass orders at the earliest after providing an opportunity of hearing to the concerned, and thereafter, these paying guest accommodations would be closed, and if necessary, demolition activities would be taken up, the counsel said.
In a detailed interim order, Justice Suraj Govindaraj issued a series of directions on the regulation, inspection and safety of PGs across the city after hearing petitions filed by owners of such accommodations.
The directions, covering 81 points, emphasise the life, health, safety and dignity of occupants, and the interests of neighbouring residents and adjoining property owners.
The judge directed the authorities to adopt a continuing system of identification, inspection, compliance and enforcement rather than treating licensing as a one-time exercise. The local authorities have to identify all PG accommodations to ascertain whether they possess a valid licence or not.
The nomenclature adopted by the operator should not, by itself, determine the regulatory character of the premises. The competent authority should also examine the substance of the activity actually carried on, Justice Govindaraj specified in his guidelines.
Onus on owner, operator & manager
The owner, operator and the person responsible for day-to-day management should comply with the statutory and regulatory obligations applicable to their roles. Where ownership and operation are vested in different persons, the inspection record should identify the owner, the lessee and the operator, the guidelines stipulated.
The operator should be responsible for the day-to-day compliance of the establishment. The operator should ensure that only permitted numbers of persons are accommodated, security and CCTV systems are functional, fire and emergency arrangements are maintained, and sanitation and hygiene requirements are complied with.
The inspection should also ascertain as to whether a sanctioned building plan exists for the facility, whether the construction conforms to the sanctioned plan and whether the use of the premises for PG accommodation is permissible.
Particular attention should be given to unauthorised mezzanine floors, roof and terrace rooms, temporary partitions, conversion of parking areas, conversion of balconies, obstruction of staircases, alteration of load-bearing structures and excessive concentration of occupants, Justice Govindaraj emphasised in his order.
The judge made it clear that if there are any violations by any of the paying guest accommodation owners or operators and no action is taken by the concerned officers, they would be personally liable for any untoward incident which may happen. The judge directed the matter to be listed again on Sept 28 for consideration.

briefs.headline: With 30% of national figures, Bengaluru paws the way in pet travel on Akasa Air
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: More than any other city in the country, Bengaluru recorded the most number of in-cabin pet travellers in Akasa Air flights. According to data shared by the airline, ferrying over 3,700 furry travelers to and from Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) since Nov 2022, when it started allowing pets inside passenger cabins.
Officially named Pets on Akasa, Bengaluru accounted for more than 30% of more than 13,500 pet journeys carried out across the airline’s pan-Indian budget fleet. It allows customers to travel on domestic flights across 28 cities with their cats and dogs in the cabin or cargo, based on their weight.
Currently only 
Air India
 and Akasa Air allows in-cabin pet travel on domestic routes with a weight limit of 10 kg (including the carrier).
The findings also reveal the growing preference among pet parents to travel with their furry companions, with Bengaluru continuing to lead demand for pet-friendly travel. Between 2024-2026, the airline informed that pet travel demand from the city grew 53%. It rose from 856 journeys in 2024 to 1,310 journeys in 2026. Dogs dominated cabin travel from and towards Bengaluru, contributing 60%, while cats accounted for 40%.
According to an Akasa Air spokesperson, five of the airline’s then most frequent pet parents were from Bengaluru. Pet parents flew mostly to Delhi, Kolkata and Guwahati with their furry companions consistently as these routes consistently ranked in top five pet travel routes during the last three financial years, contributing to over 55% of pet flights from Bengaluru.
Pet parents from Bengaluru now travel with their pets across 16 destinations, up from 10 since launch. The airline stated that cities ities like Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Guwahati, Ahmedabad pet travel is also growing in Bhubaneshwar, Pune, Lucknow, Kochi, Varanasi, Darbhanga and Calicut destinations.
“As pet ownership continues to grow, pet parents are increasingly looking to include their furry companions in leisure, family and long-distance travel. Bengaluru’s travel patterns reflect this shift, with demand extending beyond traditional metro routes to a broader mix of leisure and regional destinations,” the spokesperson added.

briefs.headline: Multiplex body opposes Karnataka’s proposed 2% cess on cinema tickets
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The Multiplex Association of India (MAI) has raised concerns over the state govt’s move to impose an additional cess of up to 2% on cinema tickets from Sept 30.
The industry body said the extra levy would push up the cost of a movie outing for viewers at a time when theatres were trying to make cinema-going more affordable and win back audiences.
According to MAI, Karnataka has close to 1,000 screens, of which around 35% are located in Bengaluru. However, the city alone accounts for nearly 50-55%, and at times up to 60%, of the state’s total box office revenue.
Kamal Gianchandani, president of MAI, said the move would hurt the exhibition sector. He pointed out that cinemas were still recovering from the aftermath of Covid, with this being the first post-pandemic year in which theatrical business has done reasonably well. He added that while govt has been pushing for ease of doing business across the country, Karnataka is adding more compliance burden on businesses instead.
“To put it in perspective, on a ticket priced at Rs 300, a 2% cess works out to Rs 6, taking the ticket price to Rs 306. As for our next steps, we’re exploring all possible options if govt goes ahead with the proposal,” Gianchandani said.
The association also argued that the cess goes against the core principle of the Goods and Services Tax (
GST
), which was introduced to do away with cascading taxes and create a simplified, unified indirect tax structure. 
Levying an additional cess on a transaction already covered under GST, MAI said, effectively amounts to a tax-on-tax, defeating the very purpose GST was meant to serve. It called for a more transparent, predictable and simplified tax framework for both consumers and businesses.
Devang Sampat, managing director of Cinepolis India, said burdening cinema-goers further was “not the appropriate way forward,” and urged the state govt to reconsider the proposed cess and look at alternative ways to fund welfare initiatives without adding to the tax load on consumers.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru Metro inducts first Titagarh-CRRC train on Green Line
briefs.bodyText:
Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. (BMRCL) has inducted the first six-coach train manufactured under its Titagarh-China Railway Rolling Stock Corporation (CRRC) rolling stock contract on the 33-km Green Line between Madavara and Silk Institute, marking another step towards clearing the backlog in the maintenance of its existing fleet.
The first train, TS16, was inducted into service on Monday. Two more trains are expected to be inducted shortly. However, the addition of the new trainsets will not immediately translate into more services or shorter waiting times for passengers.
Maintenance
According to BMRCL officials, the incoming trains are being used to facilitate the withdrawal of older trainsets for scheduled maintenance. The corporation is currently prioritising the overhaul of trains that have completed the required service period, with each trainset expected to remain under maintenance for about 15 days.
“The maintenance of metro trains is essential to ensure the safety, reliability, and availability of the fleet. While the trains are designed for a long service life, comprehensive mid-life maintenance is required to inspect, overhaul and replace components that undergo wear over years of operation,” a BMRCL official said.
Metro rolling stock typically has a service life of around 30 years, but major mid-life maintenance is carried out during the operating period to ensure that critical systems continue to function reliably. The exercise involves taking trains out of regular service for detailed inspection and scheduled overhaul, according to officials.
BMRCL had planned to use the arrival of the new trains to address the accumulated maintenance backlog. However, officials are examining the timing and pace of the programme in view of the pressure on train availability across the network.
21 trainsets
The Green Line is eventually expected to receive the complete fleet of 21 six-coach Titagarh-CRRC trains by the second quarter of 2027. The new trains are likely to be deployed exclusively on the corridor, with their maintenance to be handled at the Peenya depot.
Of the 21 trainsets, the first has now been inducted, while the remaining 20 are being manufactured at Titagarh Rail Systems’ facility in Uttarpara, West Bengal. The deployment plan is intended to simplify operations and maintenance by keeping the new fleet concentrated on a single corridor.
The arrival of the new trains will also result in a redistribution of Bengaluru Metro’s existing rolling stock. The 17 BEML trainsets currently operating on the Green Line are expected to be shifted gradually to the Purple Line, which runs between Challaghatta and Whitefield and has the highest passenger demand among the Metro corridors.
The redeployment is expected to provide additional rolling stock on the Purple Line while allowing BMRCL to maintain the Green Line with a dedicated fleet of newer trains, according to officials. The officials expect the arrangement to improve fleet availability and support capacity management on both corridors.
The new trains use Distance-To-Go (DTG) technology and have a design broadly similar to the rolling stock deployed on the Yellow Line between R.V. Road and Electronics City, which is compatible with the signalling requirements of the corridor.
The induction also marks progress in a procurement project that has faced prolonged delays. In 2019, BMRCL awarded a ₹1,578-crore contract to CRRC for the supply of 216 metro coaches. The project subsequently ran into difficulties after CRRC did not establish the manufacturing facility in India that was required under the contract.
The delays led BMRCL to issue multiple notices to the company and consider invoking a bank guarantee of ₹372 crore. The impasse was eventually addressed after CRRC partnered with Kolkata-based Titagarh Rail Systems, enabling the remaining coaches to be manufactured in India.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: Varthur-Gunjur congestion leaves schoolchildren stranded for hours
briefs.bodyText:
Routine traffic congestion in the Varthur, Gunjur and Balagere areas of east Bengaluru escalated on Thursday, leaving schoolchildren reportedly stuck in buses for over two hours even on routes as short as 5 km.
Children caught in traffic on these stretches struggled to cope with heavy dust and prolonged travel. While roads in these areas are generally congested due to limited road density and connectivity, travel time increased sharply on Thursday, which Bengaluru Traffic Police sources attributed to ongoing infrastructure works in the area.
Parents residing in a private apartment complex in Gunjur calculated the time-distance ratio from four schools to their apartment complex on Thursday. The exercise revealed that children were stuck in traffic for over two hours despite having to cover an average distance of only 6 km.
Angry parents
Pavitra Holla, a resident of Gunjur, said parents were worried as school buses were delayed by nearly two hours and, by the time the children reached home, they were exhausted. “The whole area feels like a whirlpool of mud rather than a residential locality. The kids had to sit in dust, hungry and tired,” she said.
Ramya, another resident, said that for the past week, the situation had remained the same, with travel time for schoolchildren returning home increasing to almost twice the normal duration. However, on Thursday, the worsening situation led to panic among parents, who flooded civic authorities, traffic police and schools with calls.
“The road infrastructure is miserable in the area, which could even affect the health and academic performance of children. With children being stuck for hours, they come home tired and covered in dust. Their entire schedule has changed because of poor road infrastructure,” she said. “Despite having some of the top private educational institutions in the locality, the connectivity remains subpar,” she added.
Civic works
A senior traffic officer acknowledged the issue and said civic works on State Highway 35 (Varthur-Sarjapur Road), coupled with white-topping works on Gunjur Club Road, had led to a massive diversion of traffic onto smaller roads in the area.
“With vehicles using smaller routes, and school buses also accessing the same roads, congestion has increased significantly. The roads in these neighbourhoods are already narrow, and even a small increase in vehicle volume can lead to severe traffic snarls,” the officer said. “The rain on Tuesday and Wednesday made the situation worse,” he added.
The officer said there were very few alternative routes and, therefore, even heavy vehicles had been barred from using roads in the area after 2 p.m. Despite the traffic curbs, congestion persisted, he said.

briefs.headline: Karnataka High Court lays down norms for authorities to monitor PG accommodations in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: GBA tells court that nearly 50% of the 5,000 PGs in city’s East zone are illegal
briefs.bodyText:
Expressing serious concern over the large number of paying guest (PG) accommodations operating illegally in Bengaluru, the High Court of Karnataka has issued an extensive set of guidelines to monitor, regulate, inspect and enforce safety norms for PGs across the city.
Justice Suraj Govindaraj, taking note of the seriousness of the issue and the large number of people who could be affected by any untoward incident in illegal PGs, issued comprehensive guidelines, in addition to the existing norms, to be strictly implemented by the authorities. The court was hearing petitions filed by a few PG operators challenging notices issued to them by city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).
‘Nearly 2,500 are illegal’
The GBA told the court that of around 5,000 PGs in the East Zone, nearly 2,500 are illegal and action was being initiated against them. The illegal PGs would be closed and, if necessary, buildings would be demolished if the construction violated zoning regulations or building bye-laws, the GBA informed the court.
Recognising that PG accommodation has become a vital source of temporary housing for students, employees, trainees, migrants and others seeking short- and medium-term stays in Bengaluru, the court made it clear that the guidelines were not intended to prohibit or unduly restrict lawful PG facilities, but to ensure they operate only from legally permitted premises, among other requirements.
The guidelines require authorities to identify all PG premises, whether licensed, unlicensed, operating with expired licences, or functioning under nomenclatures such as hostels, co-living establishments or service apartments. Substance, and not nomenclature, will determine the regulatory character of PGs, the court said.
The mere fact that a person owns a building shall not, by itself, make that person liable for every operational violation committed by an independent operator. Conversely, the owner shall not knowingly permit unlawful construction, unsafe structural alterations or unlawful use where such responsibility is attributable to the owner under law, the guidelines state.
As per the guidelines, authorities must verify building and land-use compliance, including sanctioned plans, zoning, unauthorised floors, terrace rooms, converted parking spaces and blocked staircases, besides sanctioned capacity, licensed capacity, number of rooms, number of beds, actual occupants and area available per occupant.
The guidelines stress that fire safety must be treated as a primary life-safety requirement, with mandatory verification of fire extinguishers, alarms, smoke detectors, emergency lighting, exits, evacuation routes, kitchen and LPG safety, and fire-vehicle access.
Privacy protection
The court emphasised occupant privacy and dignity, stating that safety regulations cannot justify arbitrary intrusion, while making it clear that CCTV cameras are prohibited in bedrooms, bathrooms, changing areas and other private spaces. PGs accommodating women or other vulnerable persons shall maintain security arrangements proportionate to the nature and occupancy of the establishment.
The court said authorities should consider establishing a unified digital database of PG accommodations while mandating a mechanism for coordination among departments.
The court also made it clear that if there are violations by PG owners or operators and no action is taken by the concerned officers, they would be personally liable for any untoward incident that may occur.
Further hearing was adjourned to September 28, with the GBA directed to file a status report detailing the number of PGs identified, the violations found and the action initiated against such breaches.

MUMBAI: With the possibility of Tata Sons' listing gaining traction, stocks of several Tata companies that hold shares of the group's holding company rallied on Thursday. Tata Chemicals jumped 6.5%, Tata Investments 5.5%, Tata Motors PV 4.5% and Tata Steel rose 2.8% while the broader market mostly closed flat.
Tata Sons' likely listing also lifted the stock price of Afcons Infrastructure, a company that belongs to Shapoorji Pallonji Group, which holds a little over 18% in Tata Sons. Some other SP group companies also saw their stock prices gain on Thursday.

Among Tata group companies, Tata Chemicals holds 2.5% of Tata Sons' equity. If Tata Sons commands a valuation of Rs 10 lakh crore, that stake would be worth Rs 25,000 crore. Several of the Tata group companies that hold stakes in Tata Sons have seen strong buying interest since RBI said late last week that Tata Sons should list.
Among the Shapoorji Pallonji Group companies, while Afcons Infra gained 3.3%, Gokak Textiles closed 9.2% up on BSE. For the debt-laden Shapoorji Pallonji Group, an IPO could offer a route to cut its roughly Rs 55,000 crore debt and relieve liquidity pressure that has dogged it for years.

MUMBAI: The Rs 22,562 crore IPO for NSE, the largest stock exchange in India in terms of turnover and profits, received bids for nearly 3.8 crore shares against about 8.9 crore shares on offer in the post-anchor bidding process. India’s two-wheeler market is seeing a shift towards premium and super-premium motorcycles with more powerful engines, more features, styling, and higher price point growing at more than 22%, a senior TVS Motor Company official said on Thursday (September 17, 2026).
The official, — Head, Business, Premium, TVS Motor Company — was speaking at the launch of TVS Motor Company’s festive-season upgrades across its Apache RTR range, including new safety, connectivity and rider-control features on the RTR 160, RTR 160 4V and RTR 200 4V, as well as updates to the Apache 310 series and TVS Ronin, Vimal Sumbly.

The company said the segment has maintained a high double-digit growth trajectory over the past two to two-and-a-half years, underscoring the shift in consumer preferences.
While premiumisation is being witnessed across consumer categories —from mobile phones and apparel to food and automobiles— it is also becoming increasingly pronounced in the two-wheeler market.
“And hence it’s so important for us to keep on capitalising on this investment that we keep on working on, to build up our portion of customer centricity, our customer obsession, and bringing in technology and disruption with a lot of speed and agility,” said Gaurav Gupta, President India 2 Wheeler Business, TVS.
On the electrification front, TVS Motor Company has seen a sharp increase in the contribution of electric vehicles, with EVs accounting for 10% of its sales last month, compared with 6.7% on a year-to-date basis last year.

briefs.headline: Tata Sons board gives Chandrasekaran 5 more years; move illegal, say Trusts
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: In an unprecedented break with its principal shareholders, 
Tata Sons
’ board Thursday voted to reappoint 
N Chandrasekaran
 as executive chairman for another five years, defying Tata Trusts, which called the resolution “a legal nullity”, exposing a split over leadership and strategy at India’s largest conglomerate.
A Tata Sons statement after the board meeting said, “Chandra acceded to the board’s request to reconsider his decision”, capping a dramatic about-turn by the chairman who had ruled himself out about a month back for lack of unanimous board-level support. The board voted by four votes to one to reappoint him. Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts, cast the sole dissenting vote while Chandra abstained.
The vote exposed differences among Trusts’ own nominee directors. Article 121A of Tata Sons’ articles requires a majority of nominee directors to back a chairman’s reappointment. Trusts vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan voted in favour; Noel voted against. That deadlock left Harish Manwani, the independent director (ID) who chaired the meeting for this proposal, to cast the deciding vote, resulting in the resolution being approved 4-1 (Anita George, an ID, and Saurabh Agrawal, group CFO & exec director, voted for Chandra).
A question mark hangs over the chairmanship though, as reappointment needs to be confirmed by shareholder approval at the next AGM.
The board also resolved to begin complying with RBI’s upper-layer NBFC rules, including a mandatory listing, and said it would seek guidance from the Trusts and other stakeholders on the issue.
Trusts, however, said they would press ahead with identifying a successor to Chandra and explore other options to avoid listing. Trusts also said they would push for a selection panel that would proceed under Tata Sons’ Articles of Association as part of an “orderly and timely leadership transition.”

briefs.headline: Chandra needs majority support from Tata Trusts' nominees: Ex-CJI
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Former chief justice of India D Y Chandrachud has opined that 
Tata Sons
 cannot validly reappoint 
N Chandrasekaran
 as executive chairman without the majority support of Tata Trusts' nominee directors. The legal opinion, obtained by Trusts, centres on the interpretation of Tata Sons' Articles of Association and the interaction between the special voting rights enjoyed by the Trusts' nominee directors and the chairman's casting vote.
Trusts chairman Noel Tata voted against reappointing Chandrasekaran while vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan backed it. The deadlock among nominee directors was broken when independent director Harish Manwani, who chaired the meeting for the resolution, exercised a casting vote.
In his opinion, Chandrachud said, "The affirmative vote of the nominee directors is an independent and standalone requirement and operates on a wholly different plane from the chairperson's casting vote which is designed to resolve a tied vote among all directors of the board taken cumulatively." He added that the chairperson's casting vote is only applicable where there is an equality of votes among two factions of the board as a whole, and not among two specific directors, whether they be nominee directors or not.
Applying this to Chandrasekaran's reappointment, Chandrachud found the resolution invalid because only one of the two nominee directors backed it. "Given that one of the two nominee directors has not voted in favour of the resolution, the requirement that a majority of nominee directors support the resolution has not been satisfied."

briefs.headline: Tata Sons must stay unlisted, should engage with RBI: Noel Tata
briefs.deck: 'Position Of Board, Trusts On Staying Private Remains Unchanged'
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Tata Trusts chairman Noel N Tata on Thursday called for 
Tata Sons
 to stay unlisted and suggested that the holding company of the salts-to-software conglomerate must engage with RBI and demanded that the decision should be reconsidered.
"...the company must explore all permissible avenues and options to avoid public listing... the letter from the regulator does not even name listing. There are other options and avenues available. The company can consider restructuring, for example. As stated above, the regulations themselves contemplate other options. All such avenues and options must be explored," he told the Tata Sons board.
While maintaining that the position of board members and the trusts on staying private remained unchanged, Noel said the holding company's chairman N Chandrasekaran had been requested to keep the trusts, the majority shareholders, informed. In Sept 2025, he said, Chandra had assured the directors that all necessary steps had been taken to maintain Tata Sons' unlisted status, which was reiterated on Feb 24.
"I do not read the assurance given... as having expired. What were the options explored by the management to avoid public listing? What was the level of engagement with the regulator on this front? The board has not been briefed on this. I call upon the chairman and the relevant officials to fully brief the board on the journey of this engagement at a subsequent meeting. 
Whatever this company now proposes to do in response to the (RBI) communication of Sept 11, 2026, it should proceed upon a position at which Tata Sons and the Tata Trusts have arrived together," he said, while insisting that Tata Trusts must be engaged at every step.
Stating that the RBI communication "reached this board without a warning", he also said that the details of what led to RBI's decision should be sought, including through RTI.
The comment came as some of the directors have indicated their support for Tata Sons to be listed.
Asserting that the Tata Group had always complied with regulations, he said in case Tata Sons had to be listed, it should seek at least three years to comply with the requirement.
Arguing against listing, Noel said Tata Sons is not a holding company in the ordinary sense as Tata Trusts, which holds around 66% stake, ploughed back the dividends received from operating companies into charity. "If Tata Sons is publicly listed, the rights of Tata Trusts as majority shareholder stand to be seriously impaired. A listed Tata Sons would be accountable to institutional and foreign shareholders whose legitimate interest is financial return," he said.
Noel said RBI norms on upper layer NBFCs allow them to move out of the enhanced regulatory framework if it is due to "voluntary strategic move to readjust operations" and if it is approved by the board.

briefs.headline: Judge Amogh Kaloti: The man who holds key to Tata dispute
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Till recently, Amogh Kaloti, who works under the law and judiciary department headed by chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, was barely known outside Maharashtra's legal circles. A low-profile district judge who was appointed Maharashtra's charity commissioner in Feb 2024, he has been pitched into the country's most high-profile corporate battle in recent years.
In May 2026, acting on a complaint by Venu Srinivasan, Kaloti directed the Sir Ratan Tata Trust to stop holding board meetings and ordered a probe into the affairs of the trusts that own 66.4% of the Tata group.
A lawyer by training and practice but now working as a bureaucrat, the 50-year-old Kaloti hails from Amravati, where he completed his education and practiced as an advocate in the district and sessions court. Both as a lawyer and as a judge, he was known to be soft-spoken, guarded and with a reputation to go strictly by the book.
Kaloti was appointed district and assistant sessions judge in 2013. He worked as district judge at Buldhana, at city civil and sessions court in Mumbai, and sessions court in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. He was posted principal district and sessions judge at Washim.
Kaloti did not respond to calls and text messages from TOI. Officials said while Kaloti is charity commissioner, the case is usually heard by an assistant commissioner or deputy commissioner. 
"After hearing, an appeal can be made before the charity commissioner. Usually it's a slow process and takes 3 to 6 months for hearings to conclude. Given the sensitive nature of the matter, even the hearings before the junior charity commissioners could take considerable time," the official said.
The charity commissioner is a quasi-judicial authority established under the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act of 1950 and plays a crucial role in administering public trusts in Mumbai. The rank is equivalent to a district judge. His powers include registering trusts, investigating financial misconduct, suspending trustees, and managing hospital charity beds.
Of three Tata-related matters before him, he has given a ruling on one. On Sept 2, he held the transfer of shares in 1989 from the Navajbai Ratan Tata Trust to Noel Tata's father Naval Tata to be legally valid. Two other complaints pending before him are by Venu Srinivasan against Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) regarding number of permanent trustees on its board, and another by Mehli Mistry against the Trusts for his removal and seeking a probe into their governance practices.

briefs.headline: UPI fee: Government, payment gateways discuss ways to stop merchants passing burden to consumers
briefs.deck: The government is currently in talks with payment platforms to ensure that merchant fees do not get passed on to consumers. Starting from October fifteenth, officials will closely monitor this situation to protect consumers. They also reassured that merchants will not incur additional GST costs once the MDR is implemented. This initiative aims to support more domestic players in the market and…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Govt is in talks with payment aggregators and platforms, which onboard merchants, to ensure that the merchant discount rate (MDR) on transactions is not passed onto consumers, finance ministry officials told reporters Thursday.
The Centre asserted that it does not expect a decline in UPI transactions or increased use of cash following its decision to charge a 0.4% merchant fee on transactions above Rs 2,000.
On Tuesday, the finance ministry said that banks have been advised to ensure merchants do not pass MDR to customers. "From Oct 15, we will monitor on a daily basis whether merchants are passing the MDR to consumers," the officials said, but did not elaborate on the steps to ensure consumers are not burdened.
Officials also argued that there will be no GST burden on merchants after MDR kicks in as the tax will be offset through input tax credit.
They also said the issue may be discussed at next month’s GST Council meeting. Countering Congress’ charges that MDR has been introduced under US pressure to aid large platforms, department of financial services took to social media and maintained that the move was meant to enable more domestic players to operate. 
It said govt had a clear policy to only allow RuPay credit cards on UPI to enable it to become the preferred choice for Indian users.
“Any foreign company operating in India would like their product to be as competitive as local ones. But if govt has kept RuPay debit cards free of MDR, how can anyone think we are acting under foreign pressure? Introducing MDR enables new players to enter and lets existing small players compete,” an official said. They stated that fully subsidizing the fast-payment system won’t ensure innovation in the sector. “As a sovereign nation, if we want to have our own institutions, some transactions have to bear the cost,” the official said.
Officials further added a dedicated fund will be set up with a contribution of 5% of the MDR collections for promoting and accelerating usage of UPI by small merchants and encouraging its sustained usage.

briefs.headline: Complex priorities: On UPI transactions, MDR charges
briefs.deck: A fear of political fallout has led to an overly complex MDR structure on UPI
briefs.bodyText:
The Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) charges announced for UPI transactions show how political considerations can dilute economic benefits. In a quest to preempt political attacks, the rate structure announced by the National Payments Corporation of India has been made overly complex. From October 15, the new rates will apply only to UPI payments of ₹2,000 or more made at merchants. As such, the charge is limited to only about 2.5% of all UPI transactions, which is a welcome limitation. Yet, within this, the rules have created different gradations. UPI payments made at small merchants earning less than ₹1 lakh a month are exempt. Those made to merchants operating in certain essential sectors will attract a flat MDR charge instead of the 0.4% applicable on other sectors. Capital market payments above ₹2,000 will attract a different MDR. These are clearly designed keeping political backlash in mind. However, they raise some important doubts among merchants, and could potentially slow the adoption of UPI in India. For example, the rules are not clear on what happens to a small merchant who crosses the ₹1 lakh a month turnover threshold, which is a low limit at today’s prices. Who is monitoring their incomes? This will either increase the compliance burden on small merchants, or involve a new mechanism for real-time transaction-checking that banks will have to develop. In the short run, it will likely result in small merchants simply refusing to accept UPI until greater clarity emerges.
The government has also instructed banks to make sure that merchants do not pass on this charge to customers. But it has not specified how banks are expected to check whether merchants tweak their prices to absorb this additional charge. A back-of-the-envelope calculation based on past trends suggests that the MDR will yield an upper limit of ₹2,400 crore of monthly revenue for the payments ecosystem. The sector-wise flat rates and reduced rates will likely result in a lower amount. The government has denied any U.S. pressure to bring these rates to favour American credit card companies. Yet, the data suggest that the benefit will largely accrue to private banks and U.S.-owned UPI apps. There is still an argument to be made for the Reserve Bank of India to foot this bill from the vast surpluses it generates every year. Maintaining vital payment infrastructure is surely a good use of these funds. However, if the government persists in implementing this charge, it should certainly simplify the structure. There is still time before its rollout. The Goods and Services Tax experience shows that rate complexity hits small businesses the hardest.

briefs.headline: Semicon India 2026: Amid ‘weaponisation’ of supply chains, PM pitches India as a ‘trustworthy’ chipmaking destination
briefs.deck: PM Modi said India’s attractiveness as an electronics manufacturing destination should be seen in the context of “weaponisation” of supply chains, and its success will benefit the entire world
briefs.bodyText:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi pitched India as a “new and trustworthy location” for electronics manufacturing, urging global chipmakers to consider the country’s potential to relieve electronics from the “weaponisation” of supply chains.
Also read | PM interacts with chip industry ahead of Semicon event
“This is not a sector where you set up a factory and the job is done,” said Mr. Modi, who inaugurated the Semicon India 2026. “Wherever semiconductor ecosystems have been built in the world, the entire ecosystem has come together only after decades of hard work. But India, with your cooperation, has worked simultaneously on chip design, manufacturing, equipment manufacturing, the materials ecosystem, testing capability, and has demonstrated success.”
Mr. Modi’s address came days after the India Semiconductor Mission’s second phase, which has an outlay of ₹1.27 lakh crore, was notified.
The Prime Minister said India is the “mother of democracy”. “When such a country succeeds in a critical industry, it strengthens the supply chain of the entire world. And today, when supply chains are being weaponised, its importance becomes much greater. We should also look at this development taking place in India from this larger perspective,” he said.
Semicon India 2026 brought together semiconductor and electronics firms from India and other countries. Speaking at the event, IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the government plans to train one lakh people who will be a “global pool of talent” and can “straightaway be employed in the factories which are coming up in India”.
Mr. Vaishnaw added that the government would target at least 200 startups and companies designing chips in India under the next phase of the country’s semiconductor mission, Semicon 2.0. He said Indian chip design firms have an established presence in the global industry, as they require little in-house manufacturing capabilities.
Global industry body SEMI’s CEO Ajit Manocha estimated that the semiconductor industry would cross $1.3 trillion this year, and $2 trillion by 2030.
Chip industry
Leaders from the semiconductor industry expressed hope in India’s trajectory and its role in their global plans. Applied Materials committed to invest $5 billion over the coming five years, to expand its R&D centre and supply chain.
“Earlier this year, we began commercial production at Sanand,” Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said. “Our current production capacity already exceeds the memory required for India’s entire laptop market … The India Semiconductor Mission, and now ISM 2.0, gave this industry a foundation it did not have before.”
Infineon CEO Jochen Hanebeck called India a “market of tremendous importance”, praising the “pace of progress across the Indian ecosystem”. Pointing to his firm increasing hiring in India by 28%, Mr. Hanebeck said that “[w]e see great potential for India to strengthen its position across the global semiconductor value chain.”
“India is evolving from a major chip consumer and chip design hub into a full-stack global semiconductor powerhouse,” Merck’s electronics CEO Benjamin Hein said.
Lam Research COO Sesha Varadarajan announced that his firm would be investing ₹10,000 crore “to establish our first silicon component manufacturing facility in the country” and that “we are increasing our partnerships with suppliers across India in specialised materials, precision components, gases, chemicals, metrology and manufacturing services.”
Wayne Allan, an executive at the Dutch firm ASML, which makes extreme ultraviolet lithography machines essential to advanced chip manufacturing, said that “India will become increasingly important globally” as the chip ecosystem develops further.
